about: This part finishes the first day and tells the second and the third. The reader warns the dead man not to be drawn to the dull white light of the gods, the path of his own delusion, and gives him a prayer to Vairocana to say after him; if he says it with devotion, he dissolves as rainbow light into Vairocana's heart and becomes a buddha in the central realm. If anger and sin make him afraid of the lights, the second day comes: the element water dawns as a white light, and from the eastern realm of Manifest Joy the blue Vajrasattva Akṣobhya appears on an elephant throne, in union with his consort and surrounded by two bodhisattvas and two goddesses. From his heart the white mirror-like wisdom pierces toward the dead man, and beside it the dull smoky light of hell. He is to trust the bright light, give up his anger and pray to Vajrasattva in the same words. Some, held back by pride, flee even from this, and on the third day the element earth dawns as a yellow light: Ratnasambhava comes from the southern realm on a horse throne with his retinue, and his yellow wisdom of sameness comes together with the dull blue light of humans. The part ends with the other way out: if the dead man recognises the light as the radiance of his own awareness, he becomes a buddha without prayer or devotion.

sentences.w: དེ་ནས་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ གྱི་ ཁྱོད་ བར་དོའི་ འཕྲང་ ལ་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ འོངས་པ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: Then, the Blessed-One Vairocana father-mother('s), you, the between's narrow-passage in, meeting for come it-is.
sentences.i: Then the Blessed One Vairocana and his consort have come to meet you in the narrow passage of the bardo.
sentences.n: The first words, de nas bcom ldan, stand at the end of p. 35, after the last sentence of the part before. 'phrang is a narrow passage, a defile on a mountain road where the traveller is at the mercy of whatever meets him; the bardo is spoken of as one. bsu ba, 'to go out to meet, to welcome', is the word for receiving a guest on the road; bsu ba la 'ongs pa, 'has come to meet'. 'ongs is the past of 'ong, 'to come'. yab yum gyi has the ending 'of' where the subject stands (the other recension has the same); it is read as marking the subject, as gyis would, and the translation passes over it.

sentences.w: རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད་ ཀྱི་ ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: Vairocana's compassion's light-ray it-is.
sentences.i: It is the light of Vairocana's compassion.
sentences.n: The blue light of the last part is meant: the bright light is the buddha's compassion reaching out to the dead.

sentences.w: ལྷའི་ འོད་ དཀར་པོ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དེ་ ལ་ དགའ་བར་ མ་ བྱེད་ཅིག༔ མ་ ཆགས་ཤིག་ མ་ ཞེན་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: The gods' light, white, lustreless, that, in, delight not do! Not be-attached! Not cling!
sentences.i: Do not take delight in the dull white light of the gods. Do not be attached to it; do not cling to it.
sentences.n: dga' bar byed, 'to take delight', with ma before the verb and cig after it: 'do not'. chags, 'to be attached', and zhen, 'to cling', are near in sense; the pair says the same thing twice for force. shig and cig are the one command particle.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཁྱོད་ ཀྱིས་ གཏི་མུག་ དྲག་པོ་ བསགས་པའི་ བག་ཆགས་ ཀྱི་ བསུ་མའི་ ལམ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: That, you by, delusion fierce accumulated's habitual-tendencies' welcomer's path it-is.
sentences.i: That is the path on which the habitual tendencies of the fierce delusion you have gathered come out to meet you.
sentences.n: gti mug, 'delusion, bewilderment', the not-seeing that is the first of the poisons of the mind; each day's dull light answers to one of them, and this one leads to the gods. bsags, 'gathered, accumulated', past of gsog: khyod kyis ... bsags pa'i, 'which you have gathered', is a clause before its noun, closed by -pa'i. bsu ma'i lam, 'the path of the welcomer': the dull light, too, comes out to receive him, as the buddhas do. In the same sentence on the second day the print has bsu ba'i lam, 'the path of welcoming'.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ ཆགས་ ན་ ནི་ ཁྱོད་ ལྷའི་ གནས་སུ་ འཁྱམས་ ཏེ༔ རིགས་ དྲུག་ཏུ་ འཁྱམས་ ནས་ ཐར་པའི་ ལམ་ དགག་པའི་ བར་ཆད་ ཡིན་པས༔
sentences.l: That to attached if, as-for: you, the gods' abode-to wander, and; kinds six-in having-wandered, liberation's path blocking's obstacle it-is-because:
sentences.i: If you are attached to it, you will wander into the abode of the gods and on among the six kinds of beings. It is an obstacle that blocks the path to liberation, so
sentences.n: lha'i gnas, 'the abode of the gods', is the highest of the six realms of rebirth (rigs drug, 'the six kinds': gods, demigods, humans, animals, hungry ghosts and hell-beings). It is pleasant, but it is still saṃsāra, and from it one falls again. thar pa, 'liberation'. dgag pa, 'to block, to stop'; bar chad, 'obstacle, interruption'. yin pas, 'because it is', runs on to the command that follows.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ མིག་ མ་ ལྟ་བར་ འོད་ མཐིང་ཁ་ བཀྲག་མདངས་ཅན་ དེ་ ལ་ མོས་པ་ གྱིས་ ལ༔
sentences.l: That at eye not looking-way, light blue lustre-radiance-having, that to, devotion do, and:
sentences.i: do not look at it. Turn with devotion to the blue light, lustrous and radiant;
sentences.n: mig ma lta bar, 'without looking with the eye'. bkrag mdangs, 'lustre and radiance' (mdangs, 'glow', as in rang mdangs); can, 'having', makes the pair a describing word. mos pa gyis la, 'make devotion, and': la after a command runs on to the next one.

sentences.w: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད་ ལ་ འདུན་པ་ དྲག་པོ་ གཏོད་ ལ༔ སྨོན་ལམ་ འདི་སྐད་ བདག་ གིས་ ལད་མོ་ གྱིས་ ལ་ གསོལ་བ་ ཐོབ་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: The Blessed-One Vairocana to aspiration fierce direct, and; prayer this-way, me by(?) imitation do, and, prayer obtain(?)!
sentences.i: direct a fierce longing to the Blessed One Vairocana, and pray, repeating this prayer after me:
sentences.n: gtod, 'to direct, to aim', as in 002. smon lam, 'aspiration-prayer', a wish spoken in the hope that it comes true. lad mo, 'imitation': lad mo byed is to copy, to repeat after someone; the reader says the prayer and the dead person says it after him. bdag gis, 'by me', is odd here; the other recension has bdag gi lad mo, 'imitation of me', and the sense is taken so. gsol ba thob cig is read, as at the end of the last part, as a guess for 'pray'.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་མ་ གཏི་མུག་ དྲག་པོས་ འཁོར་བར་ འཁྱམས་བའི་ ཚེ༔ / ཆོས་དབྱིངས་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ གསལ་བའི་ འོད་ལམ་ ལ༔ / བཅོམ་ལྡན་ རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད་ ལམ་སྣ་ དྲོངས༔ / ཡུམ་ མཆོག་ དབྱིངས་ཕྱུག་མ་ ཡིས་ རྒྱབ་ ནས་ སྐྱོར༔ / བར་དོ་ འཇིགས་པའི་ འཕྲང་ ལས་ བསྒྲལ་དུ་ གསོལ༔ / ཡང་དག་ རྫོགས་པའི་ སངས་རྒྱས་ ས་རུ་ སྐྱོལ༔
sentences.l:
Alas! Delusion fierce-by in-saṃsāra wandering's time,
the dharma-expanse wisdom bright's light-path on,
the Blessed-One Vairocana the-way lead!
The mother supreme Expanse-Lady by from-behind support!
The between fearful's narrow-passage from freeing I-pray;
the genuine perfect buddha's level-to bring!
sentences.i:
Alas! When I wander in saṃsāra through fierce delusion,
on the bright light-path of the wisdom of the expanse of reality
may the Blessed One Vairocana lead the way,
may the supreme mother, Lady of the Expanse, support me from behind.
I pray you, free me from the fearful narrow passage of the bardo
and bring me to the level of a true and perfect buddha.
sentences.n: Verse: six lines of nine syllables (the first with kyai ma before it, the same cry as kye ma), the prayer the dead person says after the reader. It comes back on each day with that day's poison, wisdom, buddha and consort. chos dbyings is chos kyi dbyings, 'the expanse of reality', shortened for the metre; its wisdom is Vairocana's. 'od lam, 'light-path': the light is the road. lam sna, 'the head of the road'; drongs is the imperative of 'dren, 'to lead': lam sna drongs, 'go before and lead the way'. rgyab nas skyor, 'hold up from behind'. yis is the 'by' ending after a vowel, used in verse. Dbyings phyug ma, 'Lady of the Expanse', is Nam mkha'i dbyings phyug ma of the last part, shortened. bsgral du gsol, 'I pray that you free': bsgral, 'to free, to deliver', with du gsol, 'I ask that'. yang dag rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas, 'the truly and perfectly awakened one', is a fixed title of a buddha (Sanskrit samyaksaṃbuddha); sa, 'ground, level', the stage reached; skyol, 'bring, deliver', the imperative of skyel. 'khyams ba'i is the print's spelling of 'khyams pa'i.

sentences.w: ཞེས་ མོས་གུས་ དྲག་པོས་ སྨོན་ལམ་ དེ་སྐད་དུ་ བཏབ་པས༔ རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད་ ཀྱི་ ཐུགས་ཀར་ འཇའ་འོད་དུ་ ཐིམ་ ནས༔ དབུས་ཕྱོགས་ སྟུག་པོ་བཀོད་པའི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་སུ༔ ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་ སྐུ་རུ་ སངས་རྒྱས་པར་ འགྱུར་རོ༔
sentences.l: So-saying, devotion-respect fierce-by, prayer thus made-because: Vairocana's heart-in as-rainbow-light dissolving, then, the centre-direction, Densely-Arrayed's realm-in, perfect-enjoyment's body-as buddha becomes.
sentences.i: When he makes this prayer with fierce devotion, he dissolves as rainbow light into the heart of Vairocana and becomes a buddha in the body of perfect enjoyment in the central realm, the Densely Arrayed.
sentences.n: zhes, 'thus', closes the quoted prayer. mos gus, 'devotion and respect'. btab pas, 'because ... made': btab is the past of 'debs, the verb for making a prayer. 'ja' 'od, 'rainbow light'; thim, 'to dissolve, to be absorbed'. Stug po bkod pa, 'Densely Arrayed' (stug po, 'thick, dense'; bkod pa, 'arranged, set out'), is the name of the buddha-field of the centre, rendered word by word. longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku, 'the body of perfect enjoyment', is the radiant form in which buddhas appear in visions, the second of the three bodies of the pilot's opening verse. sangs rgyas par 'gyur ro, 'becomes a buddha'. Where the print has de skad du, 'thus', and Vairocana's heart, the other recension has neither 'thus' nor the print's single buddha: it has the heart of Vairocana and his consort.

sentences.w: ཡང་ གལ་ཏེ་ ངོ་སྤྲད་ ཀྱང་ ཞེ་སྡང་ དང་ སྡིག་སྒྲིབ་ ཀྱི་ རྐྱེན་ གྱིས་ འོད་ དང་ ཟེར་ ལ་ སྐྲག་ ནས་ སྨོན་ལམ་ བཏབ་ ན་ ཡང་ འཁྲུལ་ ན༔
sentences.l: Again, if, face-introduced though, anger and sin-obscuration's condition by, light and rays at frightened, then, prayer made even-if, deluded if:
sentences.i: But if, though he has been pointed out, he is frightened of the lights and rays through anger and sinful obscurations, and goes astray even though he has made the prayer,
sentences.n: The print has ཞི་སྡང, a misprint for ཞེ་སྡང, 'anger', corrected here: zhi is 'peace', the print writes zhe sdang everywhere else on these pages, and the other recension has zhe sdang here. The print also has བཀྲག, 'lustre', a misprint for སྐྲག, 'frightened', corrected here: it is the same swap of skrag and bkrag as in the last part, and the other recension has skrag. zhe sdang, 'anger, hatred', is the poison of the second day. sdig sgrib, 'sin-obscuration', the veil left on the mind by harmful deeds. rkyen, 'condition, circumstance'; rkyen gyis, 'through the force of'. na yang, 'even if'. The other recension adds bros te, 'flees', after skrag nas, and has skyon, 'fault', for rkyen.

sentences.w: ཞག་ གཉིས་པ་ རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ དང་༔ དམྱལ་བའི་ ལས་ངན་ གཉིས་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ འོང་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: Day second, Vajrasattva's deity-host and hell's bad-karma, two, meeting for come, and:
sentences.i: then on the second day the host of Vajrasattva's deities and the bad karma of hell, the two together, come to meet him.
sentences.n: zhag gnyis pa, 'the second day', stands without la, 'on', which the other recension has. Rdo rje sems dpa', 'Vajra Being' (Sanskrit Vajrasattva), is the buddha of the second day; rdo rje, 'vajra', is the diamond-thunderbolt, emblem of what cannot be broken. lha tshogs, 'host of deities'. dmyal ba, 'hell'. dmyal ba'i las ngan, 'the bad karma of hell', stands where the pattern of the days leads one to expect the dull light of hell; the two that come are the bright light and the dull one.

sentences.w: ཡང་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ ནི༔ ཚེ་འདས་ ཀྱི་ མིང་ ནས་ འབོད་ ལ་ འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ་ མ་ ཡེངས་པར་ ཉོན་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Again, the face-introduction, as-for: the departed's name by calling, and, thus: O child-of-noble-family, not distracted-way listen!
sentences.i: Point him out again. Call the dead person by name and say this: O child of noble family, listen without distraction.
sentences.n: tshe 'das, 'one whose life has passed', the dead person. ming nas 'bod, 'to call by name'. 'di skad do, 'thus', with the sentence-ending -o, stands for 'say thus'. ma yengs par, 'without being distracted', as in 002.

sentences.w: ཞག་ གཉིས་པ་ ལ་ འབྱུང་བ་ ཆུ་ ཐམས་ཅད་ རྣམ་པར་ དག་པའི་ འོད་ དཀར་པོ་ འཆར་རོ༔
sentences.l: Day second on, element water all completely pure's light, white, dawns.
sentences.i: On the second day the white light dawns, the light of the element water, wholly purified.
sentences.n: 'byung ba, 'element', one of the five of which the world is made: earth, water, fire, wind and space. Each day's light is one of them made pure. rnam par dag pa, 'completely pure'. thams cad, 'all', is the print's own; the other recension has 'byung ba chu rnam par dag pa'i 'od dkar po.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ ཤར་ཕྱོགས་ མངོན་པར་དགའ་བའི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་ ནས༔ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ་ མི་བསྐྱོད་པ་ སྐུ་མདོག་ མཐིང་ཁ་ ཕྱག་ ན་ རྡོ་རྗེ་ རྩེ་ལྔ་པ་ བསྣམས་པ༔ གླང་པོ་ཆེའི་ གདན་ ལ་ བཞུགས་པ༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, the east-direction, Manifest-Joy's realm from: the Blessed-One Vajrasattva Akṣobhya, body-colour blue, hand in vajra five-pointed holding, elephant's seat on seated,
sentences.i: At that time, from the eastern realm of Manifest Joy, the Blessed One Vajrasattva Akṣobhya, blue in colour, holding a five-pointed vajra in his hand and seated on an elephant throne,
sentences.n: shar phyogs, 'the east'. Mngon par dga' ba, 'Manifest Joy' (Sanskrit Abhirati), is the buddha-field of the east. Mi bskyod pa, 'the Unshakeable' (Sanskrit Akṣobhya), is the buddha of the east; here the two names belong to one figure. rtse lnga pa, 'five-pointed'. glang po che, 'elephant'; gdan, 'seat', where Vairocana had a lion throne. bzhugs, 'to sit, to stay', the respectful word. The other recension adds mthing ka, 'blue', to the realm.

sentences.w: ཡུམ་ སངས་རྒྱས་སྤྱན་མ་ དང་ ཞལ་སྦྱར་ ནས་ རང་ ལ་ འཆར་རོ༔
sentences.l: The mother Buddha-Eye with face-joined, then, oneself to dawns.
sentences.i: in union with his consort Buddhalocanā, dawns before you.
sentences.n: Sangs rgyas spyan ma, 'Buddha-Eye' (Sanskrit Buddhalocanā), is the consort of the east: spyan, 'eye', is the respectful word, and -ma makes the name feminine.

sentences.w: བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ སའི་སྙིང་པོ་ དང་༔ བྱམས་པ་མེ་ཏྲི་ གཉིས་ ལ༔ སེམས་མ་ ལཱ་སྱ་མ་ དང་ པུཥྤེ་མ་ གཉིས་ ཀྱིས་ བསྐོར་ ནས་ འཇའ་ དང་ འོད་ ཀྱི་ ཀླུང་ ནས་ སངས་རྒྱས་ ཀྱི་ སྐུ་ དྲུག་ཏུ་ འཆར་ ནས་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: The bodhisattva Earth's-Essence and Loving-One-Maitri, two, with; the female-bodhisattvas Lāsyā and Puṣpā, two, by surrounded, then: rainbow and light's expanse from, buddha's bodies six-as dawning come.
sentences.i: Surrounded by the two bodhisattvas Kṣitigarbha and Maitreya and the two female bodhisattvas Lāsyā and Puṣpā, they come, dawning as six buddha forms out of an expanse of rainbow and light.
sentences.n: byang chub sems dpa', 'awakening-hero' (Sanskrit bodhisattva), one who has vowed to become a buddha for the sake of others. Sa'i snying po, 'Essence of the Earth' (Kṣitigarbha); Byams pa, 'the Loving One' (Maitreya), with the Sanskrit maitri after it in Tibetan letters, me tri. sems ma is short for sems dpa' ma, 'female bodhisattva'. Lāsyā, 'she of the dance', and Puṣpā, 'she of flowers', are Sanskrit names in Tibetan letters; the print spells the first ལཱ་སྱ་མ where the other recension has ལཱ་སྱེ་མ. la after the first pair is read as joining it to the second: the four together surround the buddha and his consort, and the six are these. bskor, 'surrounded'. klung is the print's spelling here of klong, 'expanse', which it writes klong on the third day. 'char nas 'ong ngo, 'they come dawning'.

sentences.w: གཟུགས་ ཀྱི་ ཕུང་པོ་ གནས་སུ་ དག་པ༔ འོད་ དཀར་པོ་ མེ་ལོང་ ལྟ་བུའི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ དཀར་ ལ་ མཚེར་བ༔
sentences.l: Form's aggregate in-its-place pure: light white, mirror like's wisdom, white and glittering,
sentences.i: The aggregate of form, pure in its own place, is the white light, the mirror-like wisdom, white and glittering,
sentences.n: gzugs, 'form', the first of the five aggregates: the body and everything that can be seen and touched. me long lta bu'i ye shes, 'the wisdom like a mirror' (Sanskrit ādarśajñāna), which shows everything and holds on to nothing, is the wisdom of this buddha. dkar la, 'white and': la between two describing words is 'and', as in gsal la dwangs. mtsher ba stands for 'tsher ba, 'glittering', which the print itself writes in the same phrase on p. 39: mtsher is no known word, and the other recension has 'tsher at every place. The print writes mtsher four times on these pages, so it may be the carver's habit; it is kept and read as 'tsher. The other recension has dag pa'i 'od dkar po, 'the white light which is the aggregate made pure'.

sentences.w: གསལ་ ལ་ དྭངས་པ་ གཅིག་ རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ ཀྱི་ ཐུགས་ཀ་ ནས་ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ མདུན་དུ་ མིག་ གིས་ མི་ བཟོད་པ་ ཙམ་དུ་ ཟུག་ ནས་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: bright and clear, one, Vajrasattva father-mother's heart from, you-yourself's in-front, eye by not bearable as-much-as, piercing comes.
sentences.i: bright and clear. It comes piercing from the heart of Vajrasattva and his consort to the space before you, so bright that your eyes can hardly bear it.
sentences.n: The first day's sentence again, with the buddha's name changed. gcig, 'one', makes it 'a light'. kyi after yab yum, where the rule gives gyi after -m, is the print's; it does not change the sense.

sentences.w: དེ་ དང་ མཉམ་དུ་ དམྱལ་བའི་ འོད་ དུད་ཁ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ ཅིག་ ཀྱང་ མདུན་དུ་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ དང་ གཤིབས་མར་ ཟུག་ ནས་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: That with together, hell's light smoke-coloured(?) lustreless, one, also, in-front, wisdom's light with side-by-side piercing comes.
sentences.i: Together with it a dull, smoky light, the light of hell, also comes piercing before you, side by side with the light of wisdom.
sentences.n: dmyal ba'i 'od, 'the light of hell', the dull light of this day, which leads to rebirth among the hell-beings. dud kha, 'smoke-coloured', from du ba, 'smoke'; kha (for ka) makes a colour word, as in mthing kha. The reading dud is uncertain: its last letter cannot be told from ང on the image, and dung, 'conch', makes no sense of a dull light; the other recension has dud ka. gshibs mar, 'side by side, alongside'.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ ཁྱོད་ ཞེ་སྡང་ གི་ དབང་ གིས་ འོད་ དཀར་པོ་ བཀྲག་མདངས་ དང་ ལྡན་པ་ དེ་ ལ་ ཁྱོད་ འཇིགས་པ་ དང༔ སྐྲག་པ་ སྐྱེས་ ནས་ བྲོས་ ཤིང་༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, you, anger's power by, light white, lustre-radiance with endowed, that, at, you, fear and terror having-arisen, fled, and:
sentences.i: At that time, driven by anger, you will be afraid and terrified of the white light, lustrous and radiant, and flee from it,
sentences.n: zhe sdang gi dbang gis, 'by the power of anger': here the day's poison drives him, where on the first day it was his bad karma. bkrag mdangs dang ldan pa, 'endowed with lustre and radiance'. The rest follows the first day word for word; the print has a second khyod, 'you', which the other recension lacks.

sentences.w: དམྱལ་བའི་ འོད་ དུ་ཁ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དེ་ ལ་ ཁྱོད་ དགའ་བའི་ འདུ་ཤེས་ སྐྱེས་ ནས་ འོང་ གི༔
sentences.l: Hell's light smoky(?) lustreless, that, toward, you, delight's notion having-arisen, come, and:
sentences.i: and a feeling of delight in the dull, smoky light of hell will arise in you, and you will go toward it.
sentences.n: du kha, here and once more below, is read as the dud kha of the sentence before; the print writes the shorter form. On this line the block is damaged, so even du is an uncertain reading. du kha by itself gives no sense, and the other recension has dud ka. Here, unlike the first day, the print has skyes nas, 'having arisen', after 'du shes, 'notion'.

sentences.w: དེ་ཙ་ན་ ཁྱོད་ འོད་ དཀར་པོ་ དཀར་ ལ་ འཚེར་བ་ གསལ་ ལ་ དྭངས་པ་ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་པར་ ཡེ་ཤེས་སུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: At-that-time, you, light white, white and glittering, bright and clear, that, at, not fearing-way, as-wisdom face-knowing do!
sentences.i: At that time do not be afraid of the white light, white and glittering, bright and clear: recognise it as wisdom.
sentences.n: The print has ལམ, a misprint for ལ་མ, corrected here: the tsheg between la and ma is missing, and only de la ma 'jigs par, 'not fearing it', gives sense; the print writes the same phrase so on the third day, and the other recension has it here. ye shes su, 'as wisdom': su marks what a thing is recognised as. Here the print writes 'tsher with its proper first letter. The other recension has bkrag la 'tsher ba, 'lustrous and glittering', for dkar la 'tsher ba.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ དད་པ་ དང་ མོས་པ་ དུང་དུང་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: That to faith and devotion longingly do!
sentences.i: Turn to it with faith and devotion, longingly.
sentences.n: As on the first day.

sentences.w: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའི་ ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ ཡིན་ནོ་ སྐྱབས་སུ་ མཆིའོ་ སྙམ་བའི་ མོས་པ་ གྱིས་ ལ་ གསོལ་བ་ ཐོབ་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: 'The Blessed-One Vajrasattva's compassion's light-ray it-is; for-refuge I-go' thinking's devotion do, and, prayer obtain(?)!
sentences.i: Think with devotion, 'This is the light of the compassion of the Blessed One Vajrasattva; I go to it for refuge', and pray.
sentences.n: The first day's words again, with Vajrasattva's name. snyam ba'i is the print's spelling of snyam pa'i; gsol ba thob cig is read, as there, as a guess for 'pray'. The other recension has thugs ka'i 'od zer, 'the light from the heart', where the print has the light of compassion.

sentences.w: དེ་ནས་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ ཁྱོད་ བར་དོའི་ འཕྲང་ ལ་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ ཡོངས་པ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: Then, the Blessed-One Vajrasattva father-mother, you, the between's narrow-passage in, meeting for come(?) it-is.
sentences.i: Then the Blessed One Vajrasattva and his consort have come to meet you in the narrow passage of the bardo.
sentences.n: The print has yongs, 'all, entirely', which makes no sense here. It is kept as printed and read as 'ongs, 'has come', the print's own word in the same sentence on the first day (the other recension has 'ong ba); whether yongs is a slip for 'ongs or for yong, a spoken form of 'ong, cannot be told, and the reading is uncertain. Where the print has the narrow passage of the bardo, the other recension has its terrors ('jigs skrag), and it begins de ni, 'that is', where the print has de nas, 'then'.

sentences.w: རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའི་ ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ གྱི་ ལྕགས་ཀྱུ་ ཡིན་པས་ མོས་པ་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Vajrasattva's compassion's light-ray's iron-hook it-is-because, devotion do!
sentences.i: It is the hook of the light of Vajrasattva's compassion: turn to it with devotion.
sentences.n: lcags kyu, 'iron hook' (lcags, 'iron'; kyu, 'hook'): the light of compassion catches hold of the one who trusts it and draws him out.

sentences.w: དམྱལ་བའི་ འོད་ དུ་ཁ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དེ་ ལ་ དགའ་བར་ མ་ བྱེད་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Hell's light smoky lustreless, that in, delight not do!
sentences.i: Do not take delight in the dull, smoky light of hell.
sentences.n: du kha is read, as above, as dud kha, 'smoky'.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཁྱོད་ ཀྱི་ ཞེ་སྡང་ དྲག་པོས་ བསགས་པའི་ སྡིག་སྒྲིབ་ ཀྱི་ བསུ་བའི་ ལམ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: That, your, anger fierce-by accumulated's sin-obscuration's welcoming's path it-is.
sentences.i: That is the path on which the sinful obscurations you have gathered through fierce anger come out to meet you.
sentences.n: khyod kyi, 'your', with zhe sdang drag pos, 'by fierce anger': the first day had khyod kyis, 'by you', in this place. sdig sgrib kyi bsu ba'i lam, 'the path of the welcoming of the obscurations'; the other recension has sdig sgrib kyis, 'by the obscurations', with the same sense.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ ཆགས་ ན་ ནི་ དམྱལ་བའི་ གནས་སུ་ ལྷུང་ སྟེ༔ སྡུག་བསྔལ་ སྲན་ མི་ བཟོད་པའི་ འདམ་དུ་ ཚུད་ དེ༔ ཐར་པའི་ དུས་ མ་ འབྱུང་ གིས༔
sentences.l: That to attached if, as-for: hell's abode-to fall, and; suffering, endurance not bearable's mire-into get, and; liberation's time not comes, and:
sentences.i: If you are attached to it, you will fall into the abode of hell and sink into a mire of unbearable suffering, and the time of liberation will not come.
sentences.n: lhung, 'to fall'. sdug bsngal, 'suffering'. sran mi bzod pa, 'whose endurance cannot be borne', is 'unbearable'; sran, 'endurance' (the other recension spells it bsran). 'dam, 'mud, mire'; tshud, 'to get into, to be caught in'; tshud de is tshud te, 'and', after -d. ma 'byung gis is awkward: ma with a verb is past or a command, and the future wants mi; the other recension has mi 'byung gi. The print is kept and read as 'will not come'. gis after the verb runs on, as gi does.

sentences.w: དེ་ ནི་ ཐར་པའི་ ལམ་ དགག་པའི་ བར་ཆད་ ཡིན་པས༔ མིག་ མ་ བལྟ་བར་ ཞེ་སྡང་ སྤོངས་ཤིག༔ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ ཆགས་ཤིག༔ མ་ ཞེན་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: That, as-for, liberation's path blocking's obstacle it-is-because: eye not looking-way, anger abandon! That to not be-attached! Not cling!
sentences.i: That is an obstacle that blocks the path to liberation, so do not look at it; give up your anger. Do not be attached to it; do not cling to it.
sentences.n: blta is the print's spelling here of lta, 'to look'. spongs is the imperative of spong, 'to give up': on this day the poison itself is to be given up, not only the light.

sentences.w: འོད་ དཀར་པོ་ གསལ་ ལ་ མཚེར་བ་ དེ་ ལ་ མོས་པ་ གྱིས་ ལ༔ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ་ ལ་ འདུན་པ་ དྲག་པོ་ གཏོད་ ལ༔ སྨོན་ལམ་ འདི་སྐད་དུ་ ཐོབ་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Light white, bright and glittering, that to devotion do, and; the Blessed-One Vajrasattva to aspiration fierce direct, and; prayer this-way obtain(?)!
sentences.i: Turn with devotion to the white light, bright and glittering, direct a fierce longing to the Blessed One Vajrasattva, and make this prayer:
sentences.n: mtsher ba is read as 'tsher ba, as above. smon lam 'di skad du thob cig has thob cig without gsol ba, and 'obtain the prayer thus' gives no clear sense; it is read, as a guess, like gsol ba thob cig, 'make this prayer'.

sentences.w: ༈ ཀྱཻ་མ་ ཞེ་སྡང་ དྲག་པོས་ འཁོར་བར་ འཁྱམས་པའི་ ཚེ༔ / མེ་ལོང་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ གསལ་བའི་ འོད་ལམ་ ལ༔ / བཅོམ་ལྡན་ རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔས་ ལམ་སྣ་ དྲོངས༔ / ཡུམ་ མཆོག་ སངས་རྒྱས་སྤྱན་མས་ རྒྱབ་ ནས་ བསྐྱོར༔ / བར་དོ་ འཇིགས་པའི་ འཕྲང་ ལས་ བསྒྲལ་དུ་ གསོལ༔ / ཡང་དག་ རྫོགས་པའི་ སངས་རྒྱས་ ས་རུ་ སྐྱོལ༔
sentences.l:
Alas! Anger fierce-by in-saṃsāra wandering's time,
the mirror wisdom bright's light-path on,
the Blessed-One Vajrasattva-by the-way lead!
The mother supreme Buddha-Eye-by from-behind support!
The between fearful's narrow-passage(?) from freeing I-pray;
the genuine perfect buddha's level-to bring!
sentences.i:
Alas! When I wander in saṃsāra through fierce anger,
on the bright light-path of the mirror-like wisdom
may the Blessed One Vajrasattva lead the way,
may the supreme mother Buddhalocanā support me from behind.
I pray you, free me from the fearful narrow passage of the bardo
and bring me to the level of a true and perfect buddha.
sentences.n: The curled mark ༈ opens the prayer as a section. It is the verse of the first day with the second day's poison, wisdom, buddha and consort. Here both buddha and consort carry -s, 'by' (rdo rje sems dpas, sangs rgyas spyan mas), as the first day's consort carried yis. me long ye shes is me long lta bu'i ye shes, shortened for the metre. bskyor is the print's other spelling of skyor, 'hold up'. The last letter of 'phrang in the fifth line cannot be told on the image from the ད of 'phrad, 'meeting', so the reading is uncertain; 'phrang is taken because the line is the same as on the first day.

sentences.w: ཞེས་ མོས་གུས་ དྲག་པོས་ སྨོན་ལམ་ དེ་སྐད་དུ་ བཏབ་པས། བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའི་ ཐུགས་ཀར་ འཇའ་འོད་དུ་ ཐིམ་ ནས༔ ཤར་ཕྱོགས་ མངོན་བར་དགའ་བའི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་སུ༔ ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་ སྐུར་ སངས་རྒྱས་པར་ འགྱུར་རོ༔
sentences.l: So-saying, devotion-respect fierce-by, prayer thus made-because: the Blessed-One Vajrasattva's heart-in as-rainbow-light dissolving, then, the east-direction, Manifest-Joy's realm-in, perfect-enjoyment's body-as buddha becomes.
sentences.i: When he makes this prayer with fierce devotion, he dissolves as rainbow light into the heart of the Blessed One Vajrasattva and becomes a buddha in the body of perfect enjoyment in the eastern realm of Manifest Joy.
sentences.n: As on the first day. btab pas is closed here by the plain stroke ། instead of ༔. mngon bar is the print's spelling of mngon par; skur is sku with -r, 'as the body', the shorter form of sku ru.

sentences.w: ཡང་ དེ་ལྟར་དུ་ ངོ་སྤྲད་ ཀྱང་ ང་རྒྱལ་ དང་ སྡིག་སྒྲིབ་ ཆེ་བའི་ གང་ཟག་ ལ་ལ་ ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ གྱི་ ལྕགས་ཀྱུ་ ལ་ འཇིགས་ ཏེ་ བྲོས་པས༔
sentences.l: Again, thus face-introduced though, pride and sin-obscuration great's persons some, compassion's light-ray's iron-hook at fearing, and, fled-because:
sentences.i: But though they have been pointed out in this way, some persons of great pride and heavy sinful obscurations are afraid of the hook of the light of compassion and flee from it. So
sentences.n: de ltar du, 'in that way'. nga rgyal, 'pride' (nga, 'I'; rgyal, 'to win'), is the poison of the third day. che ba'i gang zag, 'persons in whom ... are great'. la la, 'some'. bros pas, 'because they flee', runs on to what happens next.

sentences.w: ཡང་ ཞག་ གསུམ་པ་ ལ་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རིན་ཆེན་འབྱུང་ལྡན་ གྱི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ དང་༔ མིའི་ འོད་ལམ་ གཉིས་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ འོངས་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: Again, day third on, the Blessed-One Ratnasambhava's deity-host and humans' light-path, two, meeting for come, and:
sentences.i: on the third day the host of deities of the Blessed One Ratnasambhava and the light-path of humans, the two together, come to meet him.
sentences.n: Rin chen 'byung ldan, 'Source of Jewels' (Sanskrit Ratnasambhava; rin chen, 'precious thing, jewel'; 'byung ldan, 'having arising', a source), is the buddha of the south and of the third day. mi'i 'od lam, 'the light-path of humans', is the dull light of this day, which leads to rebirth as a human.

sentences.w: ཡང་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ ནི༔ ཚེ་འདས་ ཀྱི་ མིང་ ནས་ འབོད་ ལ་ འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ་ མ་ ཡེངས་པར་ ཉོན་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Again, the face-introduction, as-for: the departed's name by calling, and, thus: O child-of-noble-family, not distracted-way listen!
sentences.i: Point him out again. Call the dead person by name and say this: O child of noble family, listen without distraction.
sentences.n: As on the second day.

sentences.w: ཞག་ གསུམ་པ་ ལ་ འབྱུང་བ་ ས་ ཐམས་ཅད་ རྣམ་པར་ དག་པའི་ འོད་ སེར་པོ་ འཆར་རོ༔
sentences.l: Day third on, element earth all completely pure's light, yellow, dawns.
sentences.i: On the third day the yellow light dawns, the light of the element earth, wholly purified.
sentences.n: The print has འབྱུང་བས, a misprint for འབྱུང་བ་ས, 'the element earth', corrected here: the tsheg between ba and sa is missing, and only 'byung ba sa gives sense; the second day has 'byung ba chu in the same place, and the other recension has 'byung ba sa. ser po, 'yellow'.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ ལྷོ་ཕྱོགས་ དཔལ་ དང་ ལྡན་པའི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་ སེར་པོ་ ནས་ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རིན་ཆེན་འབྱུང་ལྡན་ སྐུ་མདོག་ སེར་པོ་ ཕྱག་ ན་ ནོར་བུ་ རིན་པོ་ཆེ་ བསྣམས་པ༔ རྟ་ མཆོག་ གི་ གདན་ ལ་ བཞུགས་པ༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, the south-direction, Glory-with-Endowed's realm, yellow, from: the Blessed-One Ratnasambhava, body-colour yellow, hand in jewel precious holding, horse supreme's seat on seated,
sentences.i: At that time, from the yellow southern realm called Endowed with Glory, the Blessed One Ratnasambhava, yellow in colour, holding a precious jewel in his hand and seated on a horse throne,
sentences.n: lho phyogs, 'the south'. Dpal dang ldan pa, 'Endowed with Glory' (Sanskrit Śrīmat), is the name of the southern buddha-field; dpal, 'glory, splendour'. nor bu rin po che, 'precious jewel', the gem that grants every wish. rta mchog, 'the finest horse': the seat of the south is a horse throne, as the east's was an elephant and the centre's a lion throne.

sentences.w: ཡུམ་ མཆོག་ མཱ་མ་ཀི་ དང་ ཞལ་སྦྱར་ ནས་ རང་ ལ་ འཆར་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: The mother supreme Māmakī with face-joined, then, oneself to dawning comes.
sentences.i: in union with the supreme consort Māmakī, will dawn before you.
sentences.n: Māmakī, 'She Who Is Mine', is the consort of the south; the name is Sanskrit in Tibetan letters. 'char 'ong ngo, 'comes to dawn', without the du of the first day's 'char du 'ong.

sentences.w: བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ ནམ་མཁའི་སྙིང་པོ་ དང་༔ ཀུན་ཏུ་བཟང་པོ་ གཉིས་ ལ༔ སེམས་མ་ མཱ་ལྱམ་ དང་ དྷུ་པེ་མ་ གཉིས་ ཀྱིས་ བསྐོར་ ནས༔ འཇའ་ དང་ འོད་ ཀྱི་ ཀློང་ ནས་ སངས་རྒྱས་ ཀྱིས་ སྐུ་ དྲུག་ཏུ་ འཆར་ ནས་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: The bodhisattva Sky's-Essence and All-Good, two, with; the female-bodhisattvas Mālyā and Dhūpā, two, by surrounded, then; rainbow and light's expanse from, buddha's(?) bodies six-as dawning come.
sentences.i: Surrounded by the two bodhisattvas Ākāśagarbha and Samantabhadra and the two female bodhisattvas Mālyā and Dhūpā, they come, dawning as six buddha forms out of an expanse of rainbow and light.
sentences.n: Nam mkha'i snying po, 'Essence of Space' (Ākāśagarbha). Kun tu bzang po, 'the All-Good' (Samantabhadra), is here the bodhisattva of that name, not the primordial buddha of 002. Mālyā, 'she of the garland', and Dhūpā, 'she of incense', are Sanskrit names in Tibetan letters, spelled by the print mA l+yam and d+hu pe ma (the other recension has mA le ma). The print writes nam mkha'i contracted (ནམཁའི); it is written out. sangs rgyas kyis has the ending 'by' where kyi, 'of', is meant; the print is kept and read so.

sentences.w: ཚོར་བའི་ ཕུང་པོ་ དབྱིངས་སུ་ དག་བ༔ འོད་ སེར་པོ་ མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་ ཀྱི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ སེར་ ལ་ མཚེར་བ་ ཐིག་ལེ་ དང་ ཐིག་ཕྲན་ གྱིས་ བརྒྱན་པ༔ གསལ་ ལ་ དྭངས་པ་ མིག་ གིས་ བལྟ་ མི་ བཟོད་པ་ གཅིག༔
sentences.l: Feeling's aggregate in-the-expanse pure: light yellow, sameness's wisdom, yellow and glittering, drops and small-drops by adorned, bright and clear, eye by to-look not bearable, one,
sentences.i: The aggregate of feeling, pure in the expanse, is the yellow light, the wisdom of sameness: yellow and glittering, adorned with drops and smaller drops, bright and clear, too bright for the eye to look at.
sentences.n: tshor ba, 'feeling', the second aggregate: the sense of things as pleasant, painful or neither. dbyings su dag ba, 'pure in the expanse', where the days before had gnas su, 'in its place'; dag ba is the print's spelling of dag pa. mnyam pa nyid, 'sameness' (mnyam, 'equal'; nyid, '-ness'); its wisdom (Sanskrit samatājñāna) sees all things as equal. thig le, 'drop, sphere', and thig phran, 'small drop': points of light within the light. brgyan, 'adorned'. mtsher is read as 'tsher, as before. blta mi bzod pa, 'unbearable to look at'.

sentences.w: རིན་ཆེན་འབྱུང་ལྡན་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ གྱི་ ཐུགས་ཀ་ ནས་ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ མདུན་དུ་ སྙིང་ གི་ ཐད་ཀར་ མིག་ གིས་ བལྟ་ མི་ བཟོད་པ་ ཙམ་དུ་ ཟུག་ ནས་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: Ratnasambhava father-mother's heart from, you-yourself's in-front, heart's straight-at, eye by to-look not bearable as-much-as, piercing comes.
sentences.i: It comes piercing from the heart of Ratnasambhava and his consort to the space before you, straight at your heart, so bright that your eyes can hardly look at it.
sentences.n: thad kar, 'straight toward, level with': snying gi thad kar, 'at the level of the heart'.

sentences.w: དེ་ དང་ མཉམ་དུ་ མིའི་ འོད་ སྔོན་པོ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ གཅིག་ ཀྱང་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ དང་ གཤིབ་མར་ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ སྙིང་ཁར་ ཟུག་ ནས་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: That with together, humans' light, blue, lustreless, one, also, wisdom's light with side-by-side, you-yourself's heart-at piercing comes.
sentences.i: Together with it a dull blue light, the light of humans, also comes piercing into your heart, side by side with the light of wisdom.
sentences.n: sngon po, 'blue': the print gives the light of humans this colour, here and below, where the other recension has sngon ser, 'bluish yellow'. gshib mar is the print's other spelling of gshibs mar. snying khar, 'at the heart', snying kha with -r.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ ཁྱོད་ ང་རྒྱལ་ གྱི་ དབང་ གིས་ འོད་ སེར་པོ་ བཀྲག་མདངས་ཅན་ དེ་ ལ་ འཇིགས་སྐྲག་ སྐྱེས་ ནས་ བྲོས་སུ་ འོང་ གིས༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, you, pride's power by, light yellow lustre-radiance-having, that, at, fear-terror having-arisen, fleeing come, and:
sentences.i: At that time, driven by pride, you will be afraid and terrified of the lustrous, radiant yellow light and run from it,
sentences.n: 'jigs skrag, 'fear and terror', one word. bros su 'ong, 'come to flee': the verb with su and 'ong says what will happen. gis after the verb runs on, as gi did on the second day; the other recension has 'ong zhing, 'and'.

sentences.w: མིའི་ འོད་ སྔོན་པོ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དེ་ ལ་ ཁྱོད་ དགའ་བ་ དང་༔ ཆགས་སེམས་ སྐྱེས་ ནས་ འོང་ གིས༔
sentences.l: Humans' light, blue, lustreless, that toward, you, delight and attachment-mind having-arisen, come, and:
sentences.i: and delight and desire for the dull blue light of humans will arise in you, and you will go toward it.
sentences.n: chags sems, 'a mind of attachment', desire.

sentences.w: དེ་ཙ་ན་ ཁྱོད་ འོད་ སེར་པོ་ སེར་ ལ་ མཚེར་བ་ གསལ་ ལ་ དྭངས་པ་ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་པར་ ཡེ་ཤེས་སུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་བར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: At-that-time, you, light yellow, yellow and glittering, bright and clear, that at not fearing-way, as-wisdom face-knowing do!
sentences.i: At that time do not be afraid of the yellow light, yellow and glittering, bright and clear: recognise it as wisdom.
sentences.n: The tsheg after la in de la ma 'jigs par cannot be seen on the image; the reading la ma, which the sense needs and the other recension has, is taken but marked uncertain. mtsher is read as 'tsher. shes bar is the print's spelling of shes par. The other recension describes the light differently here: gsal la dwangs ba, bkrag la dwangs ba, 'bright and clear, lustrous and clear'.

sentences.w: དེའི་ ངང་ ལ་ རིག་པ་ བྱར་མེད་ ཀྱི་ ངང་ ལ་ གློད་ ལ་ བཞོགས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: That's state in, knowing nothing-to-do's state in, loosening, rest!
sentences.i: Within it, relax and rest in the state of awareness where there is nothing to do.
sentences.n: ngang, 'state, natural condition'. byar med, 'nothing to be done' (bya, 'to do', with -r, and med, 'there is not'): awareness left as it is, without effort. glod, 'to loosen, to relax'. bzhogs shig, 'rest!, leave it!', is not the usual form: the imperative of 'jog, 'to place, to leave', is zhog, which the other recension has (lhod la zhog cig, 'relax and leave it'). The print's form is kept; the sense is clear.

sentences.w: ཡང་ན་ དེ་ ལ་ དད་པ་ དང་ མོས་པ་ དུང་དུང་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Or-else, that to faith and devotion longingly do!
sentences.i: Or else, turn to it with faith and devotion, longingly.
sentences.n: yang na, 'or else': the two ways of the book side by side, resting in awareness or praying with devotion.

sentences.w: ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ རིག་པའི་ རང་མདངས་སུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་ ན་ ནི༔ མོས་གུས་ མ་ བྱས་ སྨོན་ལམ་ མ་ བཏབ་ ཀྱང་ སྐུ་ དང་ འོད་ཟེར་ ཐམས་ཅད་ ཁྱོད་རང་ དང་ དབྱེར་མེད་དུ་ ཐིམ་ ནས་ སངས་རྒྱས་པར་ འགྱུར་རོ༔
sentences.l: You-yourself's knowing's own-radiance-as face know if, as-for: devotion-respect not done, prayer not made though, bodies and light-rays all, you-yourself with inseparable-as dissolving, then, buddha become.
sentences.i: If you recognise it as the natural radiance of your own awareness, then even without devotion and without making the prayer, all the forms and lights dissolve into you, inseparable from you, and you become a buddha.
sentences.n: rang mdangs, 'own radiance', the glow of awareness itself. ma byas, ma btab, 'not done, not made', past forms with ma. dbyer med du, 'inseparably, without being apart': the forms and lights and the one who sees them become one. The part ends here; the print line goes on with the other case, rang gi rig pa'i rang mdangs su ma shes na ni, 'if you do not recognise it ...', which begins the next part.
